issues.title: Test file separated from component
issues.description: The rule requires that for every React component file component.tsx, the test file component.test.tsx exists in the same directory. However, the test file schema-form-input-array-list.test.tsx was placed in a __tests__ subdirectory instead of being co-located with schema-form-input-array-list.tsx.
issues.rule_name: React Component Test Files Must Be Co-Located

issues.title: Drag-and-drop reordering swaps source and target indices
issues.description: The handleDragEnd function passes arguments to moveItem in the wrong order - it calls moveItem(newIndex, oldIndex) instead of moveItem(oldIndex, newIndex). This causes drag-and-drop operations to place items in the opposite position from where they're dropped. For example, dragging an item from index 2 to index 0 will incorrectly move the item at index 0 to index 2 instead, creating confusing and incorrect reordering behavior for users.

issues.title: Prefix items incorrectly included in sortable context
issues.description: The sortableKeys array is constructed from all localKeyedValues instead of excluding prefix items. The code removed the .slice(prefixItemsCount) operation, meaning prefix items (which should have fixed positions and not be draggable) are now included in the SortableContext. This allows prefix items to be moved via drag-and-drop, violating the constraint that prefix items must remain in their fixed positions and breaking the schema's structural requirements.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
// Get the keys of items that can be dragged (non-prefix items)
const sortableKeys = localKeyedValues.map((item) => item.key);

issues.title: Unused local variable `prefixItemsCount` added
issues.description: `prefixItemsCount` is introduced but never referenced anywhere in the component. This leaves unused code in the codebase, violating the rule requiring unused items to be removed.
issues.rule_name: Unused Imports Must Be Automatically Removed

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #20223 - Add drag-and-drop reordering for schema form arrays

structured_output.summary:
This PR adds @dnd-kit drag-and-drop reordering to schema form arrays. `SchemaFormInputArrayList` now wraps its items in a `DndContext` and `SortableContext`. Each `SchemaFormInputArrayItem` calls `useSortable` and shows a GripVertical handle, except prefix (tuple) items, which get `disabled: !canMove` and an empty spacer. The Move up/Move down menu items are still there.

The wiring is mostly right, but the core drop handler is broken: `handleDragEnd` calls `moveItem(newIndex, oldIndex)` with the arguments swapped. Any drag across more than one slot puts the wrong item in the wrong place. Adjacent swaps happen to come out correct, so a quick manual check can miss it. On top of that, the new `prefixItemsCount` variable is never used, which breaks the repo's Biome `noUnusedVariables: error` rule. And the behavioral tests the PR description promises (move up/down, prefix items can't move) aren't in the diff; only DOM snapshots were added.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The drag-end handler swaps its from/to indices, so the main feature reorders items wrongly for any drag longer than one step. The unused variable will also fail lint. Both should be fixed, and a test should cover the drag path, before merge.

architecture.overview:
Schema form arrays are rendered by `SchemaFormInputArrayList`, which keeps a local list of `{ key, value }` pairs. Each pair gets a stable uuid key so React keeps item identity across reorders. Every entry is rendered as a `SchemaFormInputArrayItem`. Reordering used to happen only through the item's dropdown menu (Move up/Move down), which calls `moveItem(from, to)`. That function splices the local list and sends the new values to the parent through `onValuesChange`.

This PR wraps the item list in a `DndContext` that has pointer and keyboard sensors, plus a `SortableContext` that uses the uuid keys as sortable ids. Each item registers itself with `useSortable({ id: itemKey, disabled: !canMove })`, applies the transform/transition style, and renders a drag-handle button carrying dnd-kit's attributes and listeners. Prefix (tuple) items are disabled and get a spacer instead of a handle. When a drop finishes, `handleDragEnd` turns the active and over ids back into indices and calls the same `moveItem` function the menu uses.
steps: Start at `SchemaFormInputArrayList`: `localKeyedValues` holds the `{key, value}` pairs, and `moveItem(from, to)` is the one mutation point that calls `onValuesChange`.
`useSensors` sets up a PointerSensor and a KeyboardSensor (the latter with `sortableKeyboardCoordinates`) and passes them to `DndContext`, with `closestCenter` for collision detection.
`SortableContext` receives every item's key (prefix items included) with `verticalListSortingStrategy`.
Each `SchemaFormInputArrayItem` calls `useSortable` with its `itemKey`. Prefix items pass `disabled: true`, so they can't be dragged and aren't drop targets.
When a drop finishes, `handleDragEnd` looks up the old and new indices by key and delegates to `moveItem`. The menu's Move up/down still call `moveItem` directly.

findings.title: handleDragEnd passes moveItem's arguments in reverse order
findings.fixPrompt: In `ui-v2/src/components/schemas/schema-form-input-array-list.tsx`, `handleDragEnd` (lines 130-145) calls `moveItem(newIndex, oldIndex)`, but `moveItem` takes `(from, to)`. Dragging an item more than one slot therefore produces the wrong order. Change the call to `moveItem(oldIndex, newIndex)`. Then add a unit test that drives `handleDragEnd` for a non-adjacent move, either through dnd-kit's KeyboardSensor (focus the handle, Space, ArrowDown twice, Space) or by extracting the index logic. For `[A,B,C,D]`, moving index 0 to index 3 must yield `[B,C,D,A]`.

findings.title: Unused `prefixItemsCount` variable fails Biome lint
findings.body:
`prefixItemsCount` is computed but never read anywhere:

::diff{file="ui-v2/src/components/schemas/schema-form-input-array-list.tsx" lines="45-47"}

`ui-v2/biome.json` sets `correctness.noUnusedVariables: "error"`, so this will fail `biome check` / CI.

It looks like the variable was meant to filter `sortableKeys`. The comment on line 147 says "keys of items that can be dragged (non-prefix items)", but the code maps every key. Either use it or remove it, and make the comment match. Prefix items are already excluded through `useSortable({ disabled: !canMove })`, so deleting the variable and fixing the comment is enough.
findings.fixPrompt: In `ui-v2/src/components/schemas/schema-form-input-array-list.tsx`, `prefixItemsCount` (lines 45-47) is never used, which violates the `noUnusedVariables: error` rule in `ui-v2/biome.json`. Remove it, or use it if you change how `sortableKeys` is built. Also update the comment on line 147: it says only non-prefix keys are included, but every key is passed to `SortableContext`, and prefix items are excluded through `useSortable({ disabled })` in the item component. Run `npx biome check src/components/schemas` to confirm it passes.

findings.title: Promised behavioral tests are missing; only snapshots were added
findings.fixPrompt: Add behavioral tests for array reordering in `ui-v2/src/components/schemas/schema-form.test.tsx`. Follow the existing testing-library/userEvent patterns in that file. Cover: (1) Move up / Move down menu items reorder values and the form's onValuesChange receives the new order; (2) keyboard drag-and-drop: focus a 'Drag to reorder' button, press Space, ArrowDown twice, Space, then assert the item moved two positions (this catches the reversed moveItem args in schema-form-input-array-list.tsx); (3) with `prefixItems`, prefix rows have no 'Drag to reorder' button and no Move up/down menu items.
